channel.title: FCMO AI Newsletter
channel.description: Evidence-first intelligence on the AI frontier.

item.title: ME-VLM reports a unified embodied-agent model and lower M100 prefill latency
item.description: The arXiv v2 paper presents ME-VLM, a model intended to combine embodied perception and action with multimodal agent planning and tool use. Its method trains separate agent and embodied experts, then distills them into one student with multi-teacher on-policy distillation. The authors report results on embodied, agent and transfer benchmarks. For M100 edge deployment, they report W4A8 quantization and visual-token reduction from 4,096 to 3,328 alongside prefill latency of 400 ms to 188 ms, with 96.7%/98.2% uncompressed-score retention for the 4B/35B models. These results are author-reported; this review did not reproduce them or establish broader end-to-end latency or power performance.

item.title: GittinsEval reports near-zero model-selection regret at a fraction of exhaustive benchmark cost
item.description: The arXiv v2 paper introduces GittinsEval, a Bayesian cost-aware policy for choosing which model configuration to evaluate next and when to stop. It combines Gittins-index allocation with an anytime recommendation rule for partially evaluated configurations. Replaying fixed response matrices from GSM8K, PIQA, AlpacaEval and MMLU, the authors report near-zero simple regret often using 1%–2% of exhaustive evaluation cost, with adaptive stopping commonly at 1%–10%. These are author-reported results on precomputed benchmark responses, not a live deployment study or independent reproduction. The claimed optimality is conditional on a Gaussian surrogate, independent configurations, conditionally i.i.d. item scores and predetermined costs; the paper explicitly does not provide a distribution-free finite-sample guarantee.

item.title: A preprint reports answer-aligned memory embeddings that reduce long-context inference cost
item.description: A September 22, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces Context-to-Answer-Aligned Memory Compression (CMC): it compresses document chunks into decoder-space embeddings, selects a question-relevant subset, and combines them with a local full-text window in a bounded KV cache while leaving the decoder frozen. On A100 experiments with Llama-3 8B, Mistral-7B and Gemma-2 9B across four extractive-QA benchmarks, the authors report up to 20.0% lower inference time and 20.3% lower energy at 3,000 generated tokens, plus lower peak reserved GPU memory. Results are mixed: the full-data Mistral setup loses 14.7 EM points on SQuAD and regresses on HotpotQA. The paper is an unreproduced author report; its main experiments center the local window using gold answer offsets, although an appendix tests BM25, CME-guided and midpoint alternatives.

item.title: A shared-inference cost study finds allocation rules shift tenant bills by 12–14 points
item.description: The paper introduces unalloc, which joins Kubernetes OpenCost allocations, LiteLLM gateway logs and OpenAI/Anthropic provider cost data to expose unattributed spend and reconcile it against invoices. Its accounting examples include synthetic billing fixtures: in one constructed deployment, owner labels only on leader pods left 66% of GPU spend unowned, while a fallback assigned 61% to a Helm chart label. Separately, a paper-reported H100/vLLM test found that token-based allocation assigned a retrieval-heavy tenant 12–14 percentage points more of a shared bill than equal time-share allocation across tested loads. The authors say neither meter is a ground truth; the repository describes one model and one two-minute run per load. These results show that labels, source overlap and allocation rules can change reported cost ownership, not that they change total compute expense or establish a uniquely correct cost split.

item.title: KwaiMind reports CTR-guided image editing gains in an online product-image test
item.description: Kuaishou’s KwaiMind paper combines an e-commerce image editor, an 11-task benchmark and rewards for commercial click-through rate (CTR), text accuracy and product consistency. The authors report an online A/B test in which CTR-based selection of product images increased observed CTR by about 2.44% relative to a control. In a separate offline test, the share of generated images whose predicted CTR exceeded the original image rose from 12.16% to 37.41%; this compares each checkpoint with original images, not with each other. The public code repository exposes benchmark data and evaluation commands, but the online test’s sample size and uncertainty are not reported in the inspected passage and the result has not been independently reproduced.

item.title: DolphinBench evaluates agent memory through task completion, cost and latency
item.description: A September 2026 paper introduces DolphinBench, a benchmark for testing agent memory through completion of knowledge-work tasks that depend on long conversation histories. The abstract describes three personas with roughly 500k tokens of messages each and 200 tasks per persona; each task is checked by comparing an agent run with and without the relevant history. The authors require reports of total cost and latency alongside accuracy. This is a paper-reported benchmark design, not evidence that any memory system performs better; the full protocol and independent validation were not inspected in this activation.

item.title: Source-aligned agent-memory units improve complete-evidence retrieval in a synthetic trace benchmark
item.description: A paper introduces Execution Provenance Graph Memory (EPGM) for retrieving complete supporting evidence from long agent execution histories under a fixed token budget. On 2,000 queries over 1,207 held-out ISETrace trajectories, the authors report that source-aligned provenance units improve Full Support@2048 by 19.07 points over flat 512-token windows and by 11.96 points over a per-metric oracle across four flat chunk sizes, with matched Dense-FT scoring. Holding candidate units and seed scores fixed, a graph-conditioned residual adds a smaller 4.55 points (95% CI 2.98–6.18), concentrated on queries whose evidence spans multiple events. The corpus is synthetic and the results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was performed.

item.title: On-policy distillation improves reported reasoning retention at sub-3-bit weights
item.description: A September 2026 preprint studies why quantization-aware distillation can preserve short-form answers yet leave long mathematical and code generations impaired at sub-3-bit weight precision. The authors add on-policy distillation (OPD), which samples through the deployment quantized path and applies teacher guidance to the student's own generated prefixes, alongside task verifiers. Across Qwen3 and Falcon3 models at 2.79 and 1.88 effective weight bits, they report higher math and code benchmark performance than the QAD starting checkpoints, including gains over a matched-budget continued-QAD control in all 16 reported comparisons. The released QAOPD repository links checkpoints and reproduction instructions. These remain author-reported benchmark results; independent reproduction is open. The paper also reports a material implementation caveat: OPD uses a 16-bit KV cache in the principal arms rather than the released 8-bit KV-cache configuration, a deviation the authors say favors their results.

item.title: A nested component-attribution method reports sparse, transferable circuits and a refusal edit
item.description: A September 2026 preprint proposes Matryoshka Attribution (MAttr), a learned ordering of model components based on nested masks optimized for downstream loss. The authors say it ranks first on the official Mechanistic Interpretability Benchmark leaderboard and identifies sparse, task-transferable circuits. As one application, they report that restoring 1% of Llama 3.1 8B Instruct weights to the base-model state removes refusals while maintaining capabilities. These are author claims from the preprint abstract; this activation did not inspect the full evaluation, verify the leaderboard or reproduce the intervention.

item.title: Policy-aligned critic training reports gains on mathematical reasoning and software tasks
item.description: A September 2026 preprint formalizes token-level credit using three stated regularity conditions and proposes Policy Aligned Critic Training (PACT), which trains the critic after the actor and applies importance-sampling correction. The authors report 72.87% average accuracy across four agentic mathematical-reasoning benchmarks, 8.80 and 13.16 percentage points above GRPO and PPO, respectively; on SWE-bench Verified they report 67.4%, 2.4 points above PPO. These are paper-reported results under the authors’ training and evaluation setup, not independent confirmation of a general post-training improvement.

item.title: Disaggregated quantization specializes prefill and decode for reported LLM efficiency gains
item.description: A September 2026 preprint proposes separate quantization choices for prompt prefill and token-by-token decoding, arguing that the two phases have different compute and memory bottlenecks. On released Qwen3.8-27B GGUF decoders, the authors report that an NVFP4 prefiller improved 1-bit results by 32.5 points on MMLU-Pro and 35.3 on MMMU-Pro without changing the decode checkpoint. In an 8K-prompt test on the same 27B model, SSD-offloaded disaggregated prefill reportedly reduced time to first token by 1.78× versus weight-only inference. These are author-reported results under particular model, quantization and serving conditions; no independent reproduction was performed here.

item.title: State-conditioned evidence sets improve coding-agent retrieval in author-reported tests
item.description: A September 2026 preprint defines retrieval for coding agents as recovering the evidence still missing from a captured decision state, and introduces SERBench. On 500 held-out states from 45 repositories, the authors report 73.0% complete evidence-set recovery at five source items versus 61.4% for Qwen3 embedding with reranking. A matched three-call similarity-only control reaches 66.6%, isolating a reported contribution from set-level selection. The benchmark, scorer and method code are released, while certificates remain in a separate organizer evaluator. Results are paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced here.

item.title: An energy-aware model router reports a measured accuracy–energy tradeoff across seven benchmarks
item.description: A September 2026 arXiv paper evaluates a learned router that selects among nine open-weight models using accuracy, latency, power and GPU-energy signals. On a held-out replay set of 913 questions across seven benchmarks, the authors report UniRoute accuracy of 0.618 at 2,192.2 J per answer and a KL-GRPO checkpoint at accuracy 0.609 and 1,691.9 J, about 23% lower answer energy. They describe a phase transition near 60% accuracy. The measurements use A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs and GPU energy; the headline comparison does not include router energy, which is discussed separately. This is a paper-reported result for a local-serving regime, not independent reproduction or production deployment evidence.

item.title: A robotics paper shows hidden cross-module error dependence can break downstream uncertainty calibration
item.description: A September 20, 2026 arXiv paper analyzes how uncertainty estimates from separately calibrated robotic modules can fail when combined if their errors are correlated. It studies a two-module moving-obstacle example in which position and velocity errors share fixed Gaussian marginals while their correlation varies. The authors report that individual 95% coverage stayed near nominal, but downstream coverage under an independence assumption ranged from 99.98% at correlation -0.9 to 86.46% at +0.9. In a simulated crossing controller, positive dependence increased collisions to 39.7 per 10,000 trials under the independence interface versus 8.7 with oracle joint covariance; joint-covariance estimation restored coverage near 95%, while robust bounds reduced risk at a conservatism cost. This is a controlled simulation result, not evidence of failure rates in physical robots or deployed stacks.

item.title: Trajectory-aware selection reports lower-error SWE-agent regression estimates at one-tenth benchmark size
item.description: A September 21, 2026 paper proposes selecting a small regression-test subset for software-engineering agents from prior task outcomes and sanitized trajectory embeddings. Across 76 configurations and three code-agent regression scenarios using SWE-Bench Verified and SWE-Rebench, the authors report that their 10% deterministic subset kept median resolve-rate estimation error below 5% and reduced token consumption from 3.44 billion to about 345 million in the analyzed multi-model runs. They analyze 31,779 trajectories from 58 runs across five agent frameworks and use temporal splits so selection uses earlier runs than evaluation runs. The method requires prior full-run history, dataset-specific trajectory sanitization and refresh when behavior changes; evidence is limited to code-repair benchmarks and the paper has no independent reproduction in this record.

item.title: CHOREO reports long-horizon composition of heterogeneous humanoid skills through a shared trajectory interface
item.description: A September 11, 2026 arXiv paper introduces CHOREO, which converts motion clips, pretrained RL rollouts and generated motions into a shared trajectory representation, then composes them with tracker-aware boundary matching and validated bridge motions. In a matched Unitree G1 MuJoCo benchmark of 130 fixed sequences, the authors report 124/130 successful sequences (95.4%), including 45/48 eight-action sequences (93.8%), compared with 20/48 (41.7%) for the strongest listed baseline. The paper reports one execution per task, no physical-robot tests, and closed-loop rollout for only 356 of 3,069 registered source assets. This is a potentially useful modular robotics result, not evidence of reliable real-world or open-ended humanoid autonomy.

item.title: BarrierFormer reports predictive safety control with low simulated inference latency
item.description: BarrierFormer trains a causal transformer to predict short state rollouts and enforce control-barrier constraints through a training-time safety teacher, removing online optimization at inference. The authors compare it with four reimplemented baselines across a double integrator, Dubins car and Crazyflie simulator, using 32 environments and three seeds. Their learned-dynamics variant reports 95.83%–96.88% safety on two 2D systems and 96.88% on the 3D system, with per-step batched inference around 4.79–5.12 microseconds on one workstation. This is a simulation result: training still uses a black-box simulator, performance degrades as complexity rises, and the authors warn of a potentially large simulation-to-real gap.

item.title: EgoWild2Dex reports transferring in-the-wild human video to bimanual robot manipulation with limited robot data
item.description: The authors present EgoWild2Dex, which aligns egocentric human observations with robot views and trains a dexterous manipulation policy through broad human-data pretraining, task-specific human–robot co-training and robot-domain refinement. Their EgoWild corpus contains 538.9 hours, 179,049 episodes and 125,961 task descriptions. On three long-horizon bimanual tasks, the authors report 90%–100% success using less than one hour of robot demonstrations per task; object-level success on three unseen package contents is 30%–40%. GeoFormer image alignment is reported at 7.43 ms mean latency versus 162.58 ms for a projection-and-inpainting baseline, excluding image decoding and model loading. These are author-reported results from a limited task and robot setting; the paper says the data, models and code will be released and still requires robot fine-tuning.

item.title: WaveletECO reports a specialized local model matching a frontier API on chip-repair scores at lower estimated inference cost
item.description: The authors combine a closed-loop engineering-change-order workflow with a Qwen3.5-9B model trained on repair demonstrations and action preferences. Across 22 chip designs and 594 runs, they report a mean repair score of 79.65 for INT8 and 79.63 for BF16, versus 77.44 for GPT-6 Astra under a shared execution protocol. Their cost model estimates INT8 inference at $0.00226 per task versus $0.33188 for GPT-6 Astra, about 1/147 as much, excluding EDA and idle costs. These are author-reported results from one benchmark; nine designs are held out, but the broader generalization and deployment economics remain unverified.

item.title: FoldQuantVLA reports faster low-bit inference for vision-language-action policies with small-task robot results
item.description: The authors introduce FoldQuantVLA, which keeps activation coordinate transforms consistent across calibration, quantized weight rounding and TensorRT execution. On GR00T N1.5/N1.6/N1.7 and π₀.₅, they report W4A4 projection speedups of 1.20–1.33× over floating-point TensorRT on Jetson AGX Orin and 1.25–1.52× on a desktop RTX 4070 Ti SUPER. A selective W8A8 setting for two language projections adds 1 ms to the N1.7 Orin path and reports 92.5% pooled success versus 80.0% for uniform W4A4 across 80 physical-robot trials. These are author-reported measurements: selective-precision gains were not resolved in their LIBERO controls, robot trials were small, and latency measurements used one timing run.

item.title: Apple introduces a 512 GB M5 Ultra desktop and claims faster RDMA-cluster inference
item.description: Apple’s Sept. 22, 2026 newsroom update makes Mac Studio systems with M5 Ultra available and lists configurations with up to 512 GB unified memory and 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth. Apple also says Thunderbolt 5 with RDMA enables multiple Mac Studio systems to deliver up to 3× the distributed-inference performance of one system. The product specifications and release are first-party facts; the speedup is an Apple claim whose exact model, cluster size, metric and power/cost basis are not specified in the inspected page. No independent benchmark or matched cost analysis was performed.

item.title: Conduit turns distributed RL experience handling into a runtime optimization surface
item.description: Zhang et al. present Conduit, an Experience Data Plane that separates reinforcement-learning experience ingestion, placement and delivery from framework execution. The authors report up to 97% lower exposed experience-path latency and up to 38% lower end-to-end iteration latency in RLlib tests spanning DQN, SAC and PPO workloads on an eight-actor/eight-learner setup. They also report scaling from 8 to 1,024 AMD MI250X GPUs on a fixed workload, compared with Conduit without adaptive placement, and similar convergence curves in two tested tasks. These are author-reported results from one preprint, not an independent reproduction; transfer to other workloads and full cost/energy effects remain unmeasured.

item.title: EDGEGEN reports gains from specification-derived edge-case tasks for tool-calling agents
item.description: EDGEGEN extracts compliance rules from an agent specification, combines structured rule-violation scenarios with executable database states, and uses the generated tasks for fine-tuning or harness optimization. The authors report improvement over the base model in all 18 model–benchmark comparisons across three benchmarks; on tau2-bench Airline they report relative mean-progress gains ranging from 2% to 42%, while one harness-optimization result for Gemma-4-e4b is 10% above human-curated and 30% above the base harness. Main evaluations use only 10–15 scenarios per benchmark. In a small audit, human reviewers confirmed only 6 of 10 Airline and 4 of 10 ToolSandbox runs labeled successful. These are preprint-reported results, not independently reproduced evidence of general agent reliability.

item.title: GLIDE reports that executable guardrails improve manipulation demonstrations and selected robot-policy trials
item.description: GLIDE is a framework that generates executable command guardrails from task descriptions, refines them using teleoperation trajectories and reuses them during policy execution. Across three dual-arm manipulation tasks, the authors report that GLIDE guardrails raise teleoperation success to 70%, 90% and 90%, compared with 0%, 10% and 0% under unguarded teleoperation and 20%, 60% and 60% under domain-expert hardcoded guardrails. In 10-trial policy conditions, runtime guardrails improve two success-only-trained tasks but reduce wine-serving success from 50% to 40%; mixed-quality GLIDE data with filtering reaches 70%, 60% and 60%. The paper reports a bounded physical-robot study, not general safety or broad task transfer. The authors provide a public runtime repository and demonstration datasets, which were not independently run or analyzed here.

item.title: BackTrend reports that current research agents recover few validated scientific weak signals in a retrospective benchmark
item.description: BackTrend is a retrospective benchmark built from 25 mature AI/ML topics and 66 human-validated early problem- and solution-space signals, with systems restricted to evidence available by the end of 2023. Across seven evaluated LLM, RAG and agentic systems, the authors report maximum semantic-judge F1 of 10.1% and Coverage@10 of 18.5%; deeper retrieval helps some systems, while unlimited search can reduce performance. In a sample of 100 unmatched predictions, two annotators judged 49% and 57% plausible, suggesting the reference set may omit valid signals and benchmark F1 can understate performance. The authors report a useful retrospective evaluation result, not evidence that current systems have or lack prospective scientific foresight.

item.title: Perseverance driving data supports paper-reported multimodal traversability learning on an Earth-analog rover
item.description: A September 21 arXiv paper introduces a multimodal traversability estimator trained from about 500 sols and 45 km of Mars 2020 Perseverance driving data. On 35 held-out sols, the authors report AUROC 0.874, average precision 0.878 and F1 0.758, above the strongest listed baseline (0.816, 0.802 and 0.602); means are reported across five seeds. They also describe integrating the learned hazard map into modified ENav flight software and testing it on an Earth-analog rover, primarily on flat ground with large rocks. These are paper-reported results. The linked project page says code and dataset are forthcoming; no independent reproduction or Mars deployment is established.

item.title: DUMA-Bench reports higher agent attack success in dual-control tests, with a paper–artifact mismatch
item.description: DUMA-Bench introduces executable security scenarios in which an agent and user simulator can both shape a changing environment. The paper reports higher attack success under dual-control than solo evaluation (41.1% vs 26.9%), but the linked repository README currently displays 40.3% vs 25.4% over 1,960 trials per regime. That paper–artifact difference has not been reconciled. The comparison also changes multi-turn interaction, user activity and environment evolution together, so it is a regime-level robustness gap rather than an isolated causal estimate of user influence. State assertions are deterministic, while communication assertions use GPT-4o judging.

item.title: Paired rollout schedules reduce reward noise, but do not guarantee better agent learning
item.description: The Sep. 21 arXiv paper analyzes paired, event-keyed environment schedules for group-relative reinforcement learning of tool-using agents. Its theory shows that pairing removes the shared environment-noise component from sibling reward contrasts but can still increase gradient variance under some score geometries. In a registered study using one Qwen3.5-2B agent and three seeds per design, pairing improved noisy-test success under transient tool faults by 5.1 points but missed the registered learning-curve criterion; under grader flips, the learning-curve difference was small and uncertain. A finite probe found lower gradient covariance traces, but the result is limited to eight checkpoints from two trajectories and does not establish broad learning gains.

item.title: NVIDIA pairs an agent-guided ROS 2 migration workflow with buffer-backed GPU transport
item.description: NVIDIA's Sep. 22, 2026 Isaac ROS 5.0 materials add agent-ready robotics workflows and describe using an AI-guided skill to migrate a Depth Anything 3 TensorRT node to ROS 2 Lyrical's rosidl::Buffer with a CUDA backend. ROS 2 documentation supports buffer-backed uint8[] message fields, while the upstream CUDA backend README describes same-host/same-GPU/same-user IPC and CPU fallback elsewhere. NVIDIA's tutorial presents an implementation and a verification recipe, but this review found no measured end-to-end performance result for that node migration.

item.title: A mathematical-analysis preprint reports mismatches between OpenAI’s Navier-Stokes proof and cited Lean estimates
item.description: Bastounis, Circelli and Hansen compare OpenAI’s natural-language Navier–Stokes proof with cited Lean declarations. For Lemma 8.6, equation (8.19), they report that the manuscript states an m+4 derivative estimate while the cited Lean estimate requires m+5. For pressure-flux equation (10.19), they report a different Lean bound and proof route, including an additional localized gradient norm. They note one similar auxiliary bound in the repository does not appear to be directly used in the proposed theorem, leaving the effect on the actual proof dependency chain unresolved. The authors explicitly do not claim the natural-language blow-up proof is incorrect. This remains a source-reported critique in an arXiv preprint, without independent reproduction or established specialist consensus.

item.title: EvoOntology reports gains from queryable semantic state and a regression-blocking evolution gate
item.description: EvoOntology presents an MCP-served ontology that data agents can query at runtime and refine through typed edits admitted only after paired evaluation on held-out tasks. On three data-agent benchmarks, the authors report improvements over no-ontology baselines across multiple backbones. On DDR-Bench, the paper reports a mean Trajectory-Wise gain of 12.3 percentage points from the initial ontology and another 7.7 points after self-evolution; on BIRD, initial ontology improves execution accuracy by 5.1 points and evolution adds 3.7. In an ablation averaged across four backbones, removing the paired gate lowers the final DDR-Bench score from 89.5 to 78.3 (-11.2 points), the largest drop among four loop components. These are author-reported results from a single preprint; no independent reproduction is reported here.

item.title: Cache-to-Cache reports faster cross-model communication through direct KV-cache transfer
item.description: The Cache-to-Cache (C2C) paper proposes transferring a source model’s key/value cache into a target model through a learned fuser, bypassing text generation between models. Across four question-answering benchmarks and several Qwen, Llama and Gemma combinations, the authors report 6.4–14.2% higher average accuracy than individual models and about 3.1–5.4% above text-to-text handoffs; latency was 2.5× faster on average in their tested settings. Their detailed timing table reports 3.46×, 1.51× and 14.41× speedups over text handoff for three model pairs. The fuser uses trainable pair-specific components, and scaling to many communicating models with O(N) training cost remains open. These are paper-reported results; no independent reproduction was performed.

item.title: Anthropic and Accenture announce a directly funded embedded evaluation partnership
item.description: On Sept. 18, 2026, Anthropic announced a non-exclusive partnership with Accenture’s Faculty business to evaluate and red-team models, assess alignment, and test safeguards. Each organization said it expects to invest at least $1 billion over five years to build capacity. Evaluators are intended to work inside AI companies with access comparable to employees, including observation of training and deployment decisions and direct staff interviews. Anthropic said access and reporting standards, and a settled funding model for independent evaluation, do not yet exist; it will directly fund this partnership while exploring pilots with nonprofit evaluators. This is evidence of an announced organizational model and planned investment, not evidence that evaluations are operating or independent in practice.

item.title: Anthropic reports layered defenses cut observed reasoning extraction by 10–100×
item.description: In an Oct. 12, 2026 research post, Anthropic describes layered defenses against attempts to extract Claude reasoning for unauthorized model distillation. The company reports that, after full deployment, reasoning tokens it identified as extracted by distillers on its own platform were consistently 10 to 100 times lower than before; it also says its two-stage classifier caught the extraction techniques described in its September report. This is a provider-reported operational measure, not an independent efficacy evaluation. Anthropic says it has not yet seen a highly sophisticated persistent attempt against the defenses, expects attackers to adapt, and reports integration changes, a benign-request false-positive rate below 0.1%, and charging for some blocked requests.

item.title: NostrAgent combines decentralized agent identity, scoped delegation, trust attestations and Lightning payment
item.description: The paper proposes NostrAgent, which places agent identity declarations, narrowing delegation chains and peer attestations in signed Nostr events, with Lightning HTTP 402 payment bound to agent identity. Its Python prototype reports depth-4 delegation verification at 0.0619 ms median (900 measurements) and a full L402 flow at 157.4 ms median (90 runs) on a local Docker regtest setup. The authors say 17 of 19 failure modes passed empirical tests, one was bounded analytically and one remains an architectural limitation. These are author-reported prototype results: experiments used a fixed seed on Apple Silicon/macOS with Python 3.11, and the linked replication package was not run independently. The paper also reports trust-query latency rising to 2.42 seconds at 500 synthetic nodes and identifies public attestation metadata and relay-consistency limits.

item.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder and Wonder Full with a 1M-token context and broad agent evaluations
item.description: Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full on October 12, 2026. Its research post describes both as models for personal and professional agent tasks, while the linked model card lists a 1M-token inference context and evaluations spanning agent work, coding, and general capability. The models are available through Meta's API and Muse Code, with Wonder Full limited to Muse Code subscribers. Meta reports state-of-the-art benchmark performance, but the model card says it selects the highest available result where comparable results differ and that its internally run comparisons against proprietary competitors are best-effort. This is evidence of a substantial model release and of Meta's reported evaluation, not independent confirmation of broad capability leadership; a fuller safety report is still forthcoming.

item.title: A controlled paper study reports answer-only RLVR did not improve citation faithfulness
item.description: The paper tests whether reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) for answer correctness also improves whether citations actually support model claims. Using a shared Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct base and three open-weight RLVR agents across four question-answering datasets, the authors report that the baseline produces roughly one unfaithful citation in seven questions on Wikipedia-based datasets. In fixed-context evaluation, Search-R1 and ReSearch track the base within a few percentage points, while R-Search is slightly worse; the authors state their sample could detect shifts of about seven percentage points, ruling out a large gain in this setup. A no-planting control improves on the prior measurement method. However, the evaluation is single-turn and differs from the agents' multi-turn training format; the planting-based scorer may classify obedience to altered passages as unfaithfulness, and flagged cases were not manually adjudicated. These are author-reported, bounded findings, not a general claim that RLVR cannot improve citation faithfulness.

item.title: MM-ContextFold reports lower visual context use and higher accuracy across multimodal retrieval benchmarks
item.description: MM-ContextFold keeps a persistent text-only planning context and opens temporary multimodal branches when an agent needs to inspect raw images. It folds each branch's findings back as a concise text summary, then discards the images and local branch trace. The authors first analyze approximately 10,000 trajectories and report that raw images become redundant after visual evidence has been extracted into text. Across seven multimodal agentic retrieval benchmarks and five backbones, they report 27.5% shorter working context and 6.3 percentage points higher average accuracy than a standard ReAct baseline. The main table reports means and standard deviations over three independent runs. Methods use the same underlying retrieval tools and total call budget, but preserve different native prompts and action grammars. These remain paper-reported results; no independent reproduction or deployment-cost analysis was performed.

item.title: SPHQuant reports competitive 2–3-bit VLM accuracy with faster decode than QTIP on NVIDIA GPUs
item.description: SPHQuant represents each 8D weight vector using direction and radius, allocates additional quantization precision to the radius to handle outliers, and pairs a compact direction codebook with a rotation-free CUDA inference kernel. The authors report competitive 2–3-bit task accuracy against prior quantizers across several VLMs and a 30.3% decode-throughput gain over QTIP on RTX A6000. In an added RTX 4090 test with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, batch size 1, 256 prefill tokens and 512 generated tokens, they report 288.63 tokens/s, 37.6% faster than QTIP, while using 5.35 GB GPU memory versus QTIP's 5.02 GB. These are paper-reported measurements; no independent reproduction or mobile/embedded evaluation was performed.

item.title: Harness-Zero reports distilling agent-harness behavior into a model for use under a minimal deployment scaffold
item.description: Harness-Zero uses an optimized source harness and a harnessing agent to rewrite a student's proposals into trajectories compatible with a fixed, minimal target harness; supervised fine-tuning then aims to retain useful behaviors in the model. Across SpreadsheetBench Verified, AppWorld and USPTO Retrosynthesis, the authors report that Qwen3.5-9B under the minimal harness rises from 23.3% to 44.3% macro-average task success after distillation, above 41.7% for the base model with the optimized harness still attached. The experiments also report an 81.1% versus 78.1% average for agent-as-harness versus code-as-harness in six frontier-model benchmark settings, and 82.3% recovery of 28 mined harness-induced behaviors. These are author-reported results from a single SFT seed; independent reproduction, broader transfer and full cost accounting remain open.

item.title: Reuters reports wider spreads and greater investor selectivity for AI-linked borrowers
item.description: A September 22 Reuters report describes investors becoming more selective toward AI-linked corporate debt as data-center, chip and infrastructure borrowing expands. It cites Goldman Sachs data projecting $420 billion of gross hyperscaler debt issuance in 2027, 60% above its 2026 estimate, and reports AI-related spreads around 115 basis points versus 78 basis points for broader investment-grade issuers. The article attributes selectivity chiefly to supply and concentration concerns, not default fears, and reports no resulting reduction in investment. The figures were not checked against their underlying series.

item.title: Hypernetworks report forward-only on-device LoRA personalization with competitive text-generation quality
item.description: The paper introduces a hypernetwork that maps examples of a user's prior text to a low-rank adapter (LoRA) for a small on-device language model. Adapter synthesis uses forward passes, avoiding per-user gradient descent and added prompt tokens. Across LongLaMP-3, LongLaMP-4 and LaMP-5 using Gemma3-1B-IT and Gemma1-2B-IT, the authors report ROUGE-1 results generally matching or exceeding in-context learning and PEFT alternatives. The evidence is paper-reported; the experiments do not establish production latency, energy or memory on phones, robustness for unusual users, or privacy-preserving training on real-user data.

item.title: GAE reports improved 3D consistency when generation uses geometry-native latent features
item.description: The paper proposes GAE, a compact latent derived from geometry-foundation-model features and jointly decodable to RGB, depth, camera parameters and point maps. A conditional flow model generates in that shared representation. In controlled comparisons holding generator and training protocol fixed, authors report FVD reductions of 12.7% on RealEstate10K and 23.1% on DL3DV, and half the camera-trajectory error on RealEstate10K. The paper also reports gains from metric pose scale, clean reference conditioning and representation-shaping ablations. These are author-reported results on two video datasets; no independent reproduction was performed. The measurements concern generated-view quality and geometry consistency, not physical simulation fidelity or downstream planning and control.

item.title: DataSpace reports large harness-dependent accuracy differences on heterogeneous data-agent tasks
item.description: The paper introduces DataSpace, a benchmark for data agents that must combine evidence scattered across heterogeneous task workspaces and return complete, verifiable tables. Its 410 cross-language tasks use 7,439 artifacts totaling 15.01 GB across six file and media types. In author-run comparisons, six backbones reach a best accuracy of 66.34% with DataSpace-Agent fixed; with MiMo-V2.5 fixed, five harnesses range from 30.98% to 46.34%, a 15.36-point spread. Authors also report that multimodal evidence integration and joins reduce accuracy across all tested backbones, and that 76 tasks are missed by all six. The comparison shows material harness sensitivity in this benchmark, not that harness choice generally dominates model choice. The results remain paper-reported, benchmark-bounded and unreproduced.

item.title: Embed-TTT reports task-rule structure in ARC-like embeddings, with limited out-of-distribution transfer
item.description: The paper studies whether test-time task embeddings in Vision ARC (VARC) encode the transformation rule separately from the model's execution of it. Embed-TTT freezes the backbone and first optimizes a task embedding, then freezes that embedding while fine-tuning the backbone. Across ARC-AGI-1, ConceptARC and two custom rule datasets, authors report better embedding retrieval and rule-probe scores than joint test-time training. On ARC-1, embedding-only test-time training reports 13.0% pass@1 and 17.2% pass@2, while the full two-stage method reports 49.5% and 55.2%; Full-TTT reports 48.8% and 53.8%. These are author-reported results from one study. The authors caution that embedding retrieval is indirect and can reflect memorization, and they find interpolation but not extrapolation on their parametric-rule dataset. The results motivate more diagnostic ARC-like evaluations; they do not establish general out-of-distribution reasoning.

item.title: onPanda reports faster alignment-data annotation through token-level correction
item.description: The paper presents onPanda, an interactive annotation workflow that corrects the first inappropriate token and continues generation from the revised prefix, preserving model-generated context and token-level correction traces. In a study of 21 image-description prompts with three annotators and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B rollouts, authors report median annotation time of 330 seconds per prompt versus 681 seconds for POTATO post-editing, with similar time to Argilla ranking and higher reported pairwise preference. The comparison tests whole workflows, so interface and annotation paradigm effects are confounded; its small single-task sample limits transfer. Authors also report large production-session and correction totals, which were not independently audited. A linked public Python repository contains data-conversion, supervision and benchmark code; no code execution or independent reproduction is reported here.

item.title: CARE reports improved recovery from robot failures using staged corrective demonstrations
item.description: CARE trains robot policies to recover from failures drawn from their own execution patterns. It collects unsuccessful rollouts, models stage-conditioned deviations, synthesizes failure states and corrective demonstrations, and uses a staged planner with geometric monitoring before a unified vision-language-action executor. On FSR-Bench, the authors report improved recovery over comparison methods across five simulation tasks and four real dual-arm tasks. The real-robot evaluation uses a 12-DoF SO-101 platform and 100 trials per task; the paper reports a 15.9 percentage-point gain in its real-world comparison and a 7.5-point gain on the recovery-focused FSR measure. These are author-reported results in a single paper; the research desk did not independently reproduce them.

item.title: DexTacWAM reports higher scores when tactile contact is modeled as part of the robot’s predicted world state
item.description: DexTacWAM treats fingertip tactile dynamics as part of a robot’s predicted world state rather than only as an extra policy input. It encodes each finger, compresses five tactile streams into one hand-level representation, and jointly predicts visual and tactile futures for action generation. On six contact-rich real-robot tasks, the authors report mean score 70.6 versus 38.0 for the strongest listed baseline over 20 trials per method/task. A four-task ablation reports a drop from 74.7 to 26.6 when tactile world modeling is removed while keeping tactile features and action expert. The paper also reports four hours of tactile-encoder adaptation, about 100 demonstrations per task, retention of visual prediction within 0.5 dB, and faster training/inference with compression. These are author-run results on one 22-DoF platform; camera access is matched, but the method’s relative end-effector actions differ from baseline action parameterizations, and no independent reproduction was located.

item.title: StateMem reports persistent task memory and adaptive VLA caching gains in simulation and robot tests
item.description: StateMem adds a persistent single-token memory to a vision-language-action policy: prediction-error residuals update task state, while an adaptive router reuses cached VLM prefixes and applies a correction branch. The paper reports 97.6% average success on LIBERO, 20.25% fewer prefix refreshes than full refresh, and 26.8% task success / 44.4% cumulative success on RoboMemArena among the compared single-VLA methods. Across six real-world tasks and 20 trials each on one xArm7 platform, it reports 65% average success versus 44% for π0.5 and 53% for a MemoryVLA reimplementation. Efficiency gains depend on workload: LIBERO latency falls from 156.36 to 150.78 ms, while high refresh on RoboMemArena makes routing slower than full refresh. Training used four RTX A6000 GPUs for about five days. These are author-run results, not independent validation; one-token memory and one embodiment limit transfer.

item.title: UK expands AI cyber-defence pilots and begins planning for AI-agent incidents
item.description: On 12 October 2026, the UK government announced expansion of AI cyber-defence pilots and work on preparedness for serious incidents involving autonomous AI agents. It says two pilots identified and addressed more than 1,000 potential vulnerabilities, without giving a denominator, severity distribution, validation protocol or measured change in risk. A separate June case study describes weekly hackathons scanning public code across nine government organizations: it reports 407 findings in one month, £13,000 in token costs, all critical weaknesses remediated, and manual expert checks; no exploitation evidence was identified. The relationship between that case study and the October two-pilot aggregate is unspecified. The October announcement says officials will explore possible bill changes and near-miss reporting; neither is an enacted requirement. The evidence supports government program direction and an applied human-reviewed workflow, not independently measured security effectiveness.

item.title: Feedback coding reports reliable black-box covert messages in bounded LLM tests
item.description: The paper introduces Burnashev Adaptive Posterior Matching (BAM), which uses transcript feedback, posterior matching and a confirmation phase to embed messages in generated text without giving the receiver the model’s weights or prompt. On C4 RealNews, the authors report roughly 0–0.1% error for an 8-bit payload in about 46–50 tokens across three open-weight models and 1,000 trials, versus roughly 10.5–16.8% for the strongest listed black-box baseline at 50 tokens. In separate conversational experiments, error varied by model and task: Llama-3.1 and Phi-4 stayed below 3% message error, while Qwen3-A3B-30B had 19–22% dialogue error. These are one preprint’s results; no independent reproduction was found, the implementation has computational costs, and transcript editing is outside the stated security model.

item.title: Study reports correlated post-training hiring decisions can raise modeled systemic exclusion
item.description: A preprint studies ten base and post-trained language models in a simulated U.S. hiring workflow built from sampled occupational vacancy and career-profile distributions across 76 bachelor-level occupations. The authors report that eight of ten post-trained models became less likely to callback older applicants than their base counterparts, with a median negative shift of 4.7%. They define systemic exclusion as at least nine of ten models assigning callback probability below 0.5; under this measure, the aggregate rate rises from 5.6% for base models to 17.3% after post-training, which the authors attribute mainly to more correlated decisions. These are model outputs on generated profiles, not observed hiring decisions. The data are a snapshot of U.S. online labor markets, demographic signals are simplified, and the study does not identify which post-training stage caused the changes.

item.title: MMSafe reports multilingual fine-tuning filter that lowers measured safety regressions
item.description: A preprint proposes MMSafe, which scores fine-tuning examples using both a language-shared safety-sensitive layer and language-specific layers. Across four Llama and Qwen model variants, two fine-tuning datasets and three multilingual safety benchmarks, the authors report harmful-response ratios averaging about 39% of random-filtering baselines; the method beats a prior single-layer filter on three of four model variants. They report that general and multilingual utility scores remain broadly similar in the tested settings, but results vary by dataset, model and language-specific weighting. Findings are limited to the paper’s LoRA fine-tuning and benchmark settings. The authors report releasing code, but this activation did not run it or independently reproduce the results.

item.title: CS-MoE reports cross-layer expert sharing with matched-budget perplexity gains through 12B parameters
item.description: A preprint proposes CS-MoE, which combines layer-local experts with a shared expert pool available across transformer layers. The authors report lower perplexity than dense and layer-isolated MoE baselines under matched parameter and FLOP budgets in Qwen3-backbone experiments spanning 0.6B–12B parameters. At 8B scale, one reported configuration activates 55% of physical parameters per forward pass and reaches perplexity 9.55 versus 9.75 for the dense baseline; this result is not the same as the paper’s separate 4.5-trillion-token downstream comparison. The largest reported models are 12B; routing stability, distributed-system efficiency, and post-training behavior at larger scales remain unestablished.

item.title: VideoXAgent reports competitive long-video results with query-driven expert tools
item.description: A September 11 preprint introduces VideoXAgent, an online harness that decomposes a video question and invokes specialized tools such as detection, OCR, speech recognition and frame inspection as needed. The authors report competitive performance on Video-MME-Long, LongVideoBench-Long, LVBench and MINERVA; on MINERVA they report 65.7% accuracy and about 15% of the context footprint of a 1,024-frame dense-packing baseline. The paper says its efficiency measure counts retrieved evidence and maximum agent context, not total token cost. These are author-reported benchmark results; the review did not run the system or independently reproduce them.

item.title: Pelican-Sim pairs numeric robot actions with rendered motion cues and reports downstream gains in RoboTwin
item.description: A September 10 technical report from the Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics describes Pelican-Sim 1.0, an action-conditioned video world model that combines a 28-dimensional robot-configuration vector with camera-aligned, URDF-rendered arm-motion cues, sparse mixture-of-experts layers and a distilled four-step rollout model. The authors report improved video-prediction metrics over evaluated baselines on AgiBotWorld Beta, RoboMIND and RoboTwin. In RoboTwin randomized tests, augmenting 10, 30 or 50 demonstrations per task with ten generated trajectories per demonstration raised policy success from 28.5% to 64.5%, 57.0% to 87.0%, and 70.0% to 93.0%, respectively, over five tasks and 200 unseen seeds per task. A world-model-plus-VLM evaluator reportedly ranked five policy checkpoints with Pearson correlation 0.994 after 1,000 task-specific adaptation rollouts; the test replayed the same action trajectories in the world model and simulator. The results are author-reported and primarily simulation-bounded. They do not establish physical-robot policy improvement, independent replication, or reliable closed-loop deployment under model-generated observations.

item.title: DRYLAB-Bench reports elevated assay-based biosecurity risk scores in tool-augmented model evaluations
item.description: A new preprint reports DRYLAB-Bench, an in-silico evaluation of biological-design outputs from 15 frontier language models across 30 policy-derived scenarios, scored against 187,695 pre-existing deep-mutational-scan measurements. The authors report that 67.6% of one-shot designs exceeded the average measured variant and 21.4% fell in the assay-specific highest-risk decile; under their tool-augmented iterative workflow, the top-decile share rose to 23.5% and the pooled Biosecurity Risk Score increased by 0.116 standard deviations. These are author-reported results from single-substitution assay proxies, not evidence of multi-variant organism-level outcomes, physical construction, or real-world harm. The paper’s sequential design does not isolate whether tool outputs or the additional deliberation cause the full increase, and no independent reproduction was inspected.

item.title: SpecOpt reports residue-aware optimization of predicted molecular selectivity
item.description: The preprint proposes optimizing ligand specificity by contrasting predicted residue contacts for a target and up to three off-target proteins. On a 915-compound ChEMBL-derived benchmark, the authors report that 776 compounds (84.8%) improved the target-minus-off-target AutoDock Vina score gap, with the mean changing from −0.718 to +0.472 kcal/mol and mean Tanimoto similarity of 0.72 to the starting molecules. The reported results are docking scores, not measured binding or experimental selectivity.

item.title: RoboTalk trains compact vision-language models for explicit multi-robot coordination in simulation
item.description: The revised preprint reports 7,950 FSM-validated synthetic trajectories for 53 RoboCasa-derived kitchen tasks. In closed-loop simulation, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reaches 65% success on 10 held-out tasks; adding rationale targets to the Thinking model reports up to 77%. These are author-reported simulator results, not physical-robot tests.

item.title: A cryptographic construction illustrates a limit of elicitation-based model capability audits
item.description: The paper constructs encrypted computations that can be embedded in model weights and conditionally hidden from polynomial-time elicitation under stated cryptographic assumptions. Its PyTorch proof of concept tests a small chemistry classifier: authors report resistance to supervised fine-tuning and latent adversarial training, while 8-bit gradient-based trigger search exhaustively enumerated 256 candidates and matched random search; the evaluated 16-bit query budget remained near chance. Correct-trigger chemistry accuracy was 73.5%. The authors verified individual compiled GLU units in Gemma 3 270M, but not the complete construction in a pretrained model. They also report raw compiled weights are anomalous, while obfuscation leaves possible within-layer correlation signals. This is a conditional construction and limited experiment, not evidence of hidden capabilities in deployed frontier models.

item.title: A survey of a literature-review agent reports stated trust despite mandatory checkpoints
item.description: A preprint evaluates CoSLR, a multi-agent system for systematic literature reviews with retrieval grounding and mandatory human checkpoints. In a remote, self-paced survey study, 63 participants completed a simplified workflow in about 15 minutes; recruitment used convenience channels and participants were mainly from software engineering. The authors report that 22/63 (34.9%) rated their trust in generated summaries and reports at 4 or 5 on a five-point scale for acceptance without additional checking after brief interaction. They also report that 27/63 (42.9%) rated usability highly. These are post-interaction self-reports: the study did not observe full reviews or whether participants actually skipped verification.

item.title: A paper models how distractor growth can weaken evidence retrieval in long-context models
item.description: The authors formalize “context poisoning” as competition between a decisive evidence score and the maximum score among distractors. Under a softmax retrieval abstraction, they derive a finite-sample bound in which the evidence margin needed to hold accuracy above base rate grows as Ω(√log N), where N is the effective distractor count. Controlled experiments report decreasing retrieval accuracy as context grows with hard negatives; same-format distractors produce the largest drop among the tested constructions, while retrieval gating helps only when evidence recall is preserved.

item.title: Repeated materials campaigns report a shared frontier and a common-mode structure error
item.description: A preprint compares 16 one-week autonomous materials-discovery campaigns given the same 12,499-entry metal-organic-framework database, methane-storage objective and pinned protocol. The authors report divergent search strategies but convergence near 200 cm³/cm³, with an independent calculation placing its nine best structures among agent reports. However, 15 of 16 campaigns also selected an audit-excluded incomplete structure whose missing anions created artificial pore volume. Enforced checks improved fresh-run reproduction from 1/8 to 8/8 in the tested subset but did not detectably improve conclusion validity.

item.title: A targeted SFT and RL routing study reports gains on a bounded set of enterprise analytics skills
item.description: A preprint studies how to allocate supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) for long-horizon analytics agents using production-mirroring beta APIs. It separates retrospectively observed trajectories into imitation, lift and discovery regimes, then uses teacher support and reward-observable headroom to route features to SFT, RL or further environment work. Across 18 subsequent feature-specific experiments, the diagnostic reportedly predicted 15 trajectories. On GPT-OSS 120B, targeted SFT-then-RL produced positive point estimates on seven of eight advertiser skills versus a frontier control; five gains had paired 95% confidence intervals excluding zero and one skill had a supported regression. A matched comparison reports a higher seven-skill mean delta with 43% less incremental RL compute than uniform routing.

item.title: ReAgent reports improved paper–repository consistency audits on one research-agent benchmark
item.description: ReAgent combines static inspection of paper claims against repository implementations with dynamic execution evidence. On 96 auditable repositories from a screened set of 188 AutoSOTA agent-generated paper–repository pairs, the authors report 70.83% overall audit accuracy versus 35.42% for Codex using GPT-5.4 and manually established ground truth. Ninety-two repositories were excluded, mostly because datasets or checkpoints were unavailable. The result is author-reported and limited to one platform.

item.title: DeepInstructor reports experience-grounded alignment gains on bounded idea-evaluation benchmarks
item.description: The paper proposes DeepInstructor, which retrieves dimension-specific evaluative relations from a graph built from 58,607 ICLR 2024–2025 reviews. On ExpertEval, a set of 147 ideas with expert scores, the authors report that DeepInstructor using ChatGPT-4o as backbone improves mean Hit@1 and Hit@2 agreement over standalone ChatGPT-4o by 24.4% and 29.7%. Their ICLR-derived DeepInstruct set contains 398 ideas and 289 pairs and shows mixed dimension-specific pairwise and level-accuracy changes. These are paper-reported results; the research desk did not reproduce them.

item.title: Critical-State RL selects trainable calls before optimizing multi-turn tool use
item.description: The preprint proposes diagnosing which occurrence in a multi-turn interaction is trainable before applying a local reinforcement-learning update. Nested sampling holds each candidate action fixed while resampling reward-only continuations to separate action-dependent signal from downstream noise. In a four-cell BFCL v4 multi_turn study using Gemma-4-26B-A4B, authors report that training the diagnostically selected recovery call raised missing-function accuracy from 0.14 to 0.283 ± 0.015 across four seeds on 200 paired examples; training the alternative decision call reduced it to 0.095. In the missing-argument category, the selected decision call rose from 0.435 to 0.473 ± 0.010, while the alternative recovery call reached 0.445. These are paper-reported results, not an independent reproduction.

item.title: VLM-in-Sandbox reports bounded visual evidence state for multimodal agents
item.description: The preprint presents a training-free visual workspace that registers sandbox-generated images in a ledger, keeps active visual context bounded and lets the model choose which artifacts to re-inspect. Across seven benchmarks, the authors report a 2.52 percentage-point pooled accuracy gain for GPT-4.1-mini over an append-only sandbox on 6,350 examples (95% CI 1.83–3.21), with 302 rescues and 142 regressions. A compiler-matched study on 1,260 examples reports 66.27% accuracy with 18.6% fewer total tokens than an automatic retain-all control. These are author-reported results, with heterogeneous per-benchmark effects and no independent reproduction.

item.title: ProcessLight applies step-level process supervision to traffic-signal control
item.description: ProcessLight/ STeP-PO trains an LLM traffic-signal controller with process-level credit: it scores intermediate traffic claims against observations, estimates each step’s effect on the final phase by removing it, and merges semantically similar steps into a tree for relative advantage assignment. The authors report Qwen2.5-3B trained on one synthetic flow and evaluated zero-shot in CityFlow on five real traffic-flow datasets from Jinan and Hangzhou; the method leads on most reported metrics. On two datasets, the paper reports lower average travel time than outcome-only RL, and a five-seed Holm-corrected analysis finds 81 of 90 baseline comparisons significant in its favor. The appendix also reports Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B and Llama3-8B variants and an alternate teacher, with results varying by dataset and metric. All findings remain paper-reported CityFlow simulation results for the paper’s intersection setup, not on-road deployment evidence; this review did not independently rerun the code.

item.title: Listen Then Reason weights audio test-time RL by acoustic grounding
item.description: Listen Then Reason proposes Perception-Grounded Test-Time RL (PG-TTRL) for audio-language models. It estimates each generated answer’s reliance on audio by comparing token probabilities with full audio access and with audio attention masked; a grounding margin then weights the majority-vote advantage used for unlabeled test-time RL. The authors evaluate Qwen2.5-Omni 3B and 7B on MMAR and MMAU and report higher greedy and Avg@8 scores than standard TTRL in all four model/benchmark pairings, with gains over the base model reaching 4.6 points on MMAR and 4.9 on MMAU. Majority@8 does not improve uniformly. The method adapts LoRA weights on unlabeled prompts from the benchmark test sets; added inference compute and cross-domain transfer are not established, and no independent reproduction was conducted.

item.title: Complex KDA extends Kimi Delta Attention state-transition expressivity
item.description: Complex KDA (CKDA) combines two parameter-range extensions—signed channel gates and a delta coefficient up to 2—to make Kimi Delta Attention express 2D rotations using a single diagonal-plus-rank-one recurrent transition. The paper proves exact representability for orthogonal diagonal-plus-rank-one matrices and reports finite-group state-tracking, synthetic periodic-audio and language-model experiments. The authors report stronger length extrapolation on selected synthetic tasks and language-model results comparable to KDA, not a broad demonstrated language-model advantage. Open code and committed measurements aid inspection; no independent proof audit or training reproduction was conducted.

item.title: THAW-VLA distills world-model features into a compact robot policy
item.description: THAW-VLA uses a frozen world model to produce cached training-frame features, then adds a feature-alignment loss to a compact vision-language-action policy. The teacher and projector are removed before deployment, so inference uses the undistilled student graph. The authors report a 0.8B policy moving from 95.3% to 97.9% mean success on LIBERO and from 48.2% to 50.5% on RoboCasa-GR1; they also report gains over the same student on single-arm and bimanual real-robot tasks, with 30 trials per cell. A single RTX 5090 profile is reported at 32 ms and 1.86 GB. Results remain author-reported and task-specific; independent reproduction and broader robot/task coverage are open.

item.title: PhysAI-Bench reports a 52% best score on trace-derived UAV decisions
item.description: The authors present PhysAI-Bench, a multiple-choice benchmark for foundation-model action selection from trace-derived autonomous UAV missions. Its repository describes 10,178 decisions with four candidate actions, a 35-instance human-verified development set and a 500-instance episode-disjoint held-out set. After selecting a model-specific prompt and temperature configuration, the authors report GPT-5.3 Chat at 52.00% held-out decision accuracy, the highest listed score. The reference answer is the action taken in the original mission, not necessarily the only valid or globally optimal action. The repository lists the full dataset, locked split manifests, evaluation code and model outputs as release-pending.

item.title: Victoria sets planning and resource expectations for new data centres
item.description: Victoria’s September 2026 Sustainable Data Centre Action Plan sets out planning and resource expectations for new facilities. It describes planned planning and referral controls, expects operators to offset operational electricity use through new renewable generation and storage, and assigns project-caused connection and network augmentation costs to operators. Water measures include potable-use offsets, a water-efficiency threshold, public reporting and infrastructure cost recovery. The document reports applications seeking 19,714 megalitres annually, not approved or realized demand. Several compliance details remain under development, and the Commonwealth was developing consistent mandatory standards for a later date.

item.title: CICL reports improved first-file retrieval from decision-aware reranking on a small coding benchmark
item.description: The v4 preprint presents the Counterfactual-Inspired Context Layer (CICL), which ranks candidate repository evidence by estimated effect on an agent’s next action and can compress selected context into typed memory cards. On 50 SWE-bench Verified file-retrieval instances, the authors report that Qwen3.6-Plus reranking of BM25 top-50 candidates raises hit@1 from 0.58 to 0.78 and MRR@10 from 0.634 to 0.790. Top-10 recall is 0.714 versus 0.716, and the result measures file retrieval rather than patch success. The paper’s own terminology is counterfactual-inspired; it does not claim formal causal identification.

item.title: LumoTree reports modest replay gains for speculative verification on a hybrid language model
item.description: The LumoTree v3 preprint combines path-parallel tree verification with accepted-path state replay for a recurrent-hybrid language model. On 43 fixed recorded requests, the authors report 28.13 pooled tokens/s across three runs, compared with 26.12 for five-token native multi-token prediction (MTP). In a separate 10-task coding-agent study, one attempt per arm resolved five tasks with LumoTree versus six with MTP-5, and the LumoTree arm took longer in aggregate. The paper does not claim task-completion speedup; the replay result is specific to its GB10 serving setup and small corpora.

item.title: ActGov reports benchmark reductions in indirect prompt-injection success through per-action authorization checks
item.description: A September 2026 preprint introduces ActGov, which checks each proposed tool call against a task-scoped policy before execution. The authors report lower indirect prompt-injection success on AgentDojo and AgentDyn across four model backends, with task utility retained to varying degrees. Their cross-domain transfer test also shows severe over-restriction: an AgentDojo-trained policy has 0.100 clean-task utility on AgentDyn versus 0.767 without defense. These are paper-reported benchmark results, not independent reproduction or evidence of deployment effectiveness.

item.title: Et Tu, Brute? reports wealth-conditioned recommendations by personal AI agents
item.description: In a September 2026 preprint revised to v2 on September 25, authors report 325,000 experiments across 13 personal-agent configurations and three decisions: flights, health insurance and graduate programs. Eight models systematically recommend more expensive options to wealthier users under otherwise identical requests. The reported effect can persist against an explicit cheapest-option request and when wealth is inferred from task-unrelated email; the authors describe this as benchmark evidence of wealth-conditioned recommendations, not evidence of intent or field prevalence.

item.title: OSWorld-Pro adds process-level diagnostics to computer-use evaluation
item.description: The September 2026 OSWorld-Pro preprint introduces a process-based benchmark for computer-use agents with more than 300 tasks, 2,800 sequential subgoals and over 67,000 human annotations. Authors use human-aligned language-model judges to score subgoal fulfillment through trajectories. They report Claude Opus 5 at 75.7% on OSWorld-Pro versus 83.4% on OSWorld and identify failure patterns such as irrelevant actions and click mistakes.

item.title: Available Guardrails quantifies when selective prediction can be certified
item.description: The September 2026 Available Guardrails preprint studies whether finite calibration data can certify target precision for every reporting unit in a selective prediction system. It uses exact-binomial inversion and dynamic programming to expose the trade-off among certified precision, subgroup granularity and served traffic. In author-run evaluations, split-sample partition selection gains a reported mean 0.060 coverage over support balancing, with a positive direction in 59 of 60 model effects across three intent-routing datasets and two architectures; a naive estimator captures only 0.005 of a reported 0.157 population-known opportunity.

item.title: RegimeAbstain estimates multi-hop retrieval failure from query and ANN structure
item.description: The September 2026 RegimeAbstain preprint models retrieval confidence from query and approximate-nearest-neighbor structure, without an extra language-model call, then abstains on risky multi-hop retrievals. Across three benchmarks and two retrieval architectures, the authors report confident-wrong-answer rates of 14.5%–62.1%. On MuSiQue with an LLM-judge pipeline, they report reducing that rate from 39.5% to 20.6% at 50% coverage, with expected calibration error 0.035.

item.title: AutoViewMem organizes long-term conversational memory into learned semantic views
item.description: The September 2026 AutoViewMem preprint proposes learning low-overlap semantic views from conversational traces and using them to structure memory at write time, followed by offline consolidation and ordinary top-K retrieval. The authors report improved long-horizon question answering and personalization over memory baselines on LoCoMo and PersonaMem with Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-14B.

item.title: A compositional benchmark exposes the reuse–forgetting tradeoff in continual robot world models
item.description: A September 18, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces a benchmark for continual world models in robot manipulation. Six simulated task curricula end with compositions of earlier action and perception primitives, separating reuse on a new task from forgetting on earlier tasks. The authors evaluate DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 with fine-tuning, replay, EWC and PackNet, plus a modular Prismatic World Model. In a diagnostic with an encoder pretrained on demonstrations from all benchmark tasks and then frozen, PWM reports mean forgetting score 3.85 and forward-transfer score 36.18 across six suites, compared with 34.97 and 38.11 for TD-MPC2 using that same encoder; lower forgetting and higher forward transfer are better. Without this privileged encoder, PWM is reported on par with TD-MPC2. The study is limited to simulation, three seeds, selected model settings, and no controlled parameter or compute budgets; it does not establish physical-robot performance.

item.title: A preprint reports that persistent spatial guidance improved object acquisition in a small blind-user study
item.description: A September 18, 2026 arXiv preprint describes Touvigation, a phone-based assistive object-acquisition system that combines vision-language interpretation with persistent local 3D tracking. Its audio guidance shifts from room-scale orientation and step counts to body-relative reaching cues and tactile verification. In a within-subject study, the authors report 48 successful trials out of 48 with Touvigation, versus 28/48 with ByteDance's Doubao assistant and 41/48 without AI; they also report faster completion and lower workload. The finding is bounded to 12 blind adults, two unfamiliar rooms and short-term use after familiarization. Participants were from one regional community and one severity category; the system depends on a LiDAR-equipped chest-mounted iPhone, initial room scanning, stable tracking and cloud processing. The study has not been independently replicated.

item.title: Australia consults on conditions for AI training, creator rights and infrastructure investment
item.description: On September 17, 2026, Australia’s Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet opened a consultation on proposed national standards for large data centres and conditions for frontier AI training. The paper links the policy design to attracting investment while managing energy, water, community and workforce effects; it also says copyright treatment, creator protections, local research capability and compute access matter to AI training policy. The consultation asks how the government should secure local contributions and protect creators while providing regulatory certainty. It does not announce a final policy, create a copyright exception or document a company-specific bargain. Submissions closed October 9, 2026, and the paper says responses and stakeholder engagement will inform later standards.

item.title: A preprint reports that separating environmental facts from task procedures can help evolving agents
item.description: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint proposes TTSE, which evolves environmental facts (FACT) separately from task-conditioned procedures (TIP), using interaction evidence to revise or retire both kinds of rule. The paper frames representation errors and execution errors as distinct contributors to agent failure and evaluates the framework on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, GDPevo, SOPBench and PinchBench. Authors report gains over selected baselines and an end-to-end PinchBench score of 0.7822 versus 0.7439 across three runs. In the SOPBench comparison, the reported dual-track gain over a single-track Bayesian-memory ablation is 2.99 percentage points over 892 tasks, but warehouse inspection contributes 78% of the gain; without that domain the reported gap is 0.67 points, and dangerous-goods tasks slightly favor single-track. The preprint reports no independent reproduction; its GDPevo dual-versus-TIP ablation is not formally significance-tested, and induced rules lack a structured verification gate.

item.title: A preprint reports label-free visual grounding gains at inference, but not from pilot distillation
item.description: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint evaluates a model's sensitivity to question-relevant image crops as a label-free visual-evidence signal. On one 191-example V*Bench evaluation using three Qwen vision-language models, the authors report that selecting among 16 candidate crops raised fine-grained answer accuracy from about 70% to 85% and localized target regions 4.4–5.1 times above chance. Combining the evidence-gap signal with model confidence improved correctness prediction in the reported test. The authors also tested gated self-distillation: on HR-Bench, no gating, trajectory gating and token gating all scored below the base model, with more aggressive gating performing worse. The inference and training findings come from different tests and should remain separate. Results are author-reported, unreproduced and limited to one small benchmark; the crop search also requires 16 forward passes per example.

item.title: A preprint reports GPT-6 Astra leading a simulated robot benchmark, with sharp control limits
item.description: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint reports an evaluation of GPT-6 Astra acting directly as a robot manipulation policy, without task-specific fine-tuning or a learned motor policy in the control path. Across 42 RoboDojo simulation tasks and 2,100 trials, the authors report 22.48% average success and a score of 28.97, above the 40 public policies in their September 10 leaderboard snapshot. The result is uneven: Astra trails the top policy on precision, long-horizon and memory axes, while GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash perform much worse in the same reported interface. The authors say they stopped real-robot trials after unsafe actions damaged equipment; the paper does not establish real-world reliability or safe control. These are preprint-reported results without independent reproduction, and the public-policy runs did not receive the wiki-derived task text supplied to the LLMs.

item.title: BabelArena tests agent execution across 23 languages and reports resource-linked failure gaps
item.description: A September 20 preprint introduces BabelFlow, a workflow for adapting agent benchmarks across languages while preserving links among prompts, tools, environments and evaluators, and releases BabelArena with 16,146 instances across 23 languages. In a 40-task Chinese ablation, the authors report fewer broken references and behavioral mismatches than independent translation, at higher token cost. Their five-model evaluation reports lower task success and language consistency in the low-resource language group, with distinct tool-use/control-flow failures and increased input-token use in sampled tasks. These are paper-reported findings; translation validity, independent reproduction and generalization remain open.

item.title: MemCalib measures whether language-model agents give stored facts the right influence
item.description: An October 8 v3 preprint introduces MemCalib, a benchmark that scores whether each fact in an agent’s stored memory should be ignored, used as bounded support, or allowed to control the answer. The authors report 15,000 examples across health, general assistance and coding. On its 1,500-example test set, the highest listed exact calibration is 28.40% for GPT-5.6-SOL; most evaluated models more often over-use memory than under-use it. The authors report that MemCalib-RL improves Qwen3-8B atom-use accuracy on this benchmark and transfers to a 150-query RPEval subset, while increasing under-use relative to the base model. Results are paper-reported and rely on constructed memory examples and rubric-guided model judging; real-world transfer is unknown.

item.title: Loopjacking paper reports agent approval reused for materially changed operations in tested product paths
item.description: A September 2026 preprint defines Loopjacking as product logic applying a human decision for an operation A to a materially different operation B. In purposively selected tests, the author reports post-approval substitution in seven sampled Agno AgentOS releases and 12 sampled in-memory LangGraph Agent Server compositions with a declared authorization policy, plus an incomplete shell-command approval representation in OpenClaw 2026.2.23. OpenClaw 2026.2.24 rejected the tested mismatch. OpenAI Agents SDK 0.22.0 and 0.22.2 served as negative controls that rejected same-call mutation.
